response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Make `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` concrete before using it as a handler

Affected:
- src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11-12

Explanation:
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract methods: `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. That makes `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` an abstract class.

`Detector.detector_handler` instantiates `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For any detector whose type is the metric alert group type, that call will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. The exception escapes `process_detectors` and aborts processing of every detector in the batch.

Before this change, the class was a safe no-op that returned `[]`.

Fix options:
- Keep a concrete stub until the real implementation exists, or
- Implement the three abstract methods with safe no-op defaults.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):
    def get_dedupe_value(self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]) -> int:
        return 0  # TODO

    def get_group_key_values(
        self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]
    ) -> dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]:
        return {}  # TODO

    def build_occurrence_and_event_data(
        self, group_key: DetectorGroupKey, value: int, new_status: PriorityLevel
    ) -> tuple[IssueOccurrence, dict[str, Any]]:
        raise NotImplementedError
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Guard the conversion from `DetectorPriorityLevel` to `PriorityLevel`

Affected:
- src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:298-301

Explanation:
`PriorityLevel(new_status)` relies on every non-OK `DetectorPriorityLevel` value having an exact numeric match in `PriorityLevel`. The definition of `DetectorPriorityLevel` is not in this diff, so I could not confirm this. If the two enums diverge (for example, a new detector level is added), the call raises `ValueError` mid-evaluation, after `enqueue_state_update` has already been called. Use an explicit mapping, or at least a clear error.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
_DETECTOR_TO_ISSUE_PRIORITY = {
    DetectorPriorityLevel.LOW: PriorityLevel.LOW,
    DetectorPriorityLevel.MEDIUM: PriorityLevel.MEDIUM,
    DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH: PriorityLevel.HIGH,
}
...
result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(
    group_key, value, _DETECTOR_TO_ISSUE_PRIORITY[new_status]
)
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Make the mock occurrence depend on the inputs it receives

Affected:
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:244-275
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:190-192
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:489-491
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:509-511
- tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:536-545

Explanation:
`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`, so the tests pass even though they compute expectations with the wrong value:
- `6` is used where the real value is `10`, `100`, or `8`.

As a result, the tests cannot detect the handler passing the wrong value to the hook.

In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the occurrence is built for group key `"val1"` (which affects the fingerprint), but `expected_result` uses `"group_key"`. The expectations are inconsistent; whether this fails depends on test code outside the shown hunk.

Fix:
- Have the mock encode `value` (for example, in `evidence_data`).
- Build expectations with the actual group key and value.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
occurrence = IssueOccurrence(
    ...,
    evidence_data={"value": value},
    ...
)
# and in tests:
build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 10, PriorityLevel.HIGH)
build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "group_key", <actual value>, PriorityLevel.HIGH)
~~~

## 4) Severity: INFO | Type: Doc
Title: Update the stale `evaluate` docstring

Affected:
- src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:229-231

Explanation:
The docstring still says `evaluate` "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". It now returns a dict keyed by group key. Update the docstring to match the new contract.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
"""
Evaluates a given data packet and returns a dict of `DetectorGroupKey` -> `DetectorEvaluationResult`.
...
"""
~~~
